t: Peninsular War: French forces under Jean-de-Dieu Soult attacked the British amphibious evacuation under Sir John Moore at Corunna in Galicia, Spain.
After standing for only 15 years, the Theatre Royal, Drury Lane, the third building in London of that name, burned down.
Napoleonic Wars: The British invasion of Martinique ended with the unconditional surrender of French admiral Louis Thomas Villaret de Joyeuse, beginning a five-year occupation of the island.
Napoleonic Wars: British forces captured the French frigate Niémen in the Bay of Biscay.
Napoleonic Wars: The War of the Fifth Coalition began with the Austrian invasion of Bavaria, then a client state of France.
Napoleonic Wars: A hastily assembled Royal Navy fleet launched an assault against the main strength of the French Atlantic Fleet; an incomplete victory led to political turmoil in Britain.
Napoleonic Wars: After a three-day chase, the French ship D'Hautpoul was captured off Puerto Rico by a British squadron under Alexander Cochrane.
War of the Fifth Coalition: French general Louis-Nicolas Davout defeated an Austrian force in Lower Bavaria, allowing him to rejoin the main French army.
War of the Fifth Coalition: Commanded by Napoleon, Franco-German forces defeated a reinforced Austrian corps at the Battle of Abensberg.
Napoleon's French forces defeated Archduke Charles' Austrian army at the Battle of Wagram, the decisive confrontation of the War of the Fifth Coalition.
As part of the Persian Gulf campaign, a British flotilla arrived at and launched an amphibious assault on Ras Al Khaimah.
Napoleonic Wars: In the Bay of Bengal, a squadron of French frigates captured three ships carrying recruits for the armies of the East India Company.
Napoleonic Wars: While transporting supplies to Guadeloupe, French commodore François
American physician Ephraim McDowell performed the world's first removal of an ovarian tumor.
